history.body: Hi, I came across the Pearl Residences ad. We’re looking to upgrade from our rental sometime this year. What’s the project like?

Pearl Residences is a freehold condominium in Seberang Jaya. The Phase 1 homes are 900 sq ft, with 3 bedrooms, 2 bathrooms and a balcony—so you’d have flexibility for a separate work or guest room as you move on from renting. One important timing point: completion is expected in Q4 2029, so it won’t be ready to move into this year. When you say you’re looking to upgrade this year, do you mean you need to move this year, or are you planning to buy this year even if the home completes later?
We don’t need to move this year; we’re hoping to buy within the next year if we find the right place. So Q4 2029 is the expected completion date, right?

Yes—Phase 1 is expected to be completed in Q4 2029. Since you’re hoping to buy within the next year rather than move this year, that could work if you’re comfortable planning ahead and waiting for completion. It may be worth seeing whether the layout feels right for your next step beyond renting; I can help arrange a viewing if you’d like.

Maybe, but Q4 2029 feels quite far and we’re not in a rush to move. Our rental feels small with our little one, so we’d need to feel sure the layout would actually give us more usable space before planning a visit.

That’s fair—900 sq ft alone doesn’t prove it’ll feel roomier than your rental. The Type A layout avoids a long internal corridor, with open-plan living, dining and kitchen space plus a small storage area. That could give you a more connected family area while keeping the bedrooms separate, but I’d want to compare the actual plan before saying it offers more usable space. I’ll check the approved plan’s room dimensions. Do you know roughly how large your current rental is?
I’m not sure of the exact size—it’s a small two-bedroom rental. The living area gets crowded with our little one’s things and day-to-day stuff.

That’s a useful comparison point. With a third bedroom, you could potentially keep some of your little one’s things out of the shared area, while the open-plan living, dining and kitchen keeps family time connected. I wouldn’t assume it will feel roomier just from the 900 sq ft, though—the room dimensions will matter for whether it actually solves the crowding.
That could help if the third room gives us somewhere to keep the everyday things. I’d want to look at the actual plan with my partner first, though; we still have time before completion.

That makes sense—reviewing the plan together is a good way to judge whether the third room could take some of your little one’s everyday things and help keep the shared area clearer. The room dimensions will matter, so I don’t want to promise it will solve the crowding based on the 900 sq ft alone. I’ll follow up with the confirmed plan details before you decide whether a visit is worthwhile; there’s no need to rush it.
